ANSWER:
How a `POST /v1/<tool>` request gets from the socket to the tool. All of the HTTP code is in `src/http/mod.rs` and needs the `remote` feature.

1. **`worker`** (`src/http/mod.rs:278`): each worker thread has its own `mcp::Session` and an optional `OAuth` handle. It loops on `server.recv()` and passes every request to `handle`.
2. **`handle`** (`src/http/mod.rs:376`): reads the body (refusing anything over `MAX_BODY` or not UTF-8 with a 413) and checks the `Origin` header with `origin_allowed` (403 if not allowed). Then it calls `route` and builds the response, including the CORS headers.
3. **`route`** (`src/http/mod.rs:436`): splits the path from the query string and trims any trailing `/`. It marks `/mcp` and `/v1/*` as protected. Before any route is matched, it runs `if protected && method != Method::Options && !authorized(req, shared, oauth) { return unauthorized(oauth); }` (lines 441–444). If that passes, the match arm `(Method::Post, p) if p.starts_with("/v1/") => rest(&p[4..], query, body, session)` (line 504) picks up the request.
4. **The Authorization check is `authorized`** (`src/http/mod.rs:342`). With `AuthMode::None` it returns true. Otherwise it reads the `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header and accepts the token if it matches the static token (compared with `oauth::same`) or is a live OAuth token (`OAuth::check_access`). If the check fails, `unauthorized` (line 355) returns a 401 with a `WWW-Authenticate` challenge.
5. **The hand-off to the shared MCP dispatcher is `rest`** (`src/http/mod.rs:511`). It parses the body as a JSON object of tool arguments (400 if it isn't one) and sets `args["format"] = "json"` unless the URL has `?format=text`. Then it calls **`session.call(tool, &args)`** and turns the result into the HTTP reply. An error starting with "unknown tool" becomes a 404; any other error becomes a 400.
6. **`Session::call`** (`src/mcp.rs:441`) is the shared tool dispatcher. It checks whether memory and data tools are enabled, including read-only memory (`--memory-tools recall`), then runs the named tool. The `/mcp` endpoint reaches the same session through `Session::handle_body` (`src/mcp.rs:659`), and stdio MCP uses the same session too.

In short: `worker` → `handle` → `route` (calls `authorized`) → `rest` → `Session::call`.

CONFIDENCE: high
